ddsim.device.pn_diode.pn_diode.Na: how many acceptors per cubic centimetre on the p side [cm^-3]. Range 1e14 to 1e19, log. Below 1e14 the p side is barely doped at all, and above 1e18 the textbook built in potential it's checked against starts to drift.
ddsim.device.pn_diode.pn_diode.Nd: how many donors per cubic centimetre on the n side [cm^-3]. Range 1e14 to 1e19, log. Same limits as Na, for the same reasons.
ddsim.device.pn_diode.pn_diode.length: how long the diode is [cm]. Range 1e-5 to 1e-3, log. That's 0.1 um to 10 um, from just enough room either side of the junction up to a long diode.
ddsim.device.pn_diode.pn_diode.junction: where the p side ends and the n side starts [cm], measured from the left and inside the length. Range 1e-5 to 9e-5.
ddsim.device.pn_diode.pn_diode.n_nodes: how many mesh points the diode is cut into [1]. Range 51 to 1001. The low end is deliberately coarse, so you can see what too few points across the depletion region does.
ddsim.device.pn_diode.pn_diode.h_min: the smallest mesh spacing, right at the junction [cm]. Range 1e-8 to 1e-6, log. The default of 1 nm easily resolves a 1e16 junction.
ddsim.device.pn_diode.pn_diode.anode_voltage: voltage on the p side contact [V]. Range -5 to 1. Much above 1.3 V forward, the solver can't find a starting guess for this device.
ddsim.device.pn_diode.pn_diode.cathode_voltage: voltage on the n side contact [V]. Range -5 to 1. Same limits as the anode.

ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.substrate_doping: net doping of the silicon [cm^-3]. Negative means p-type, so -1e16 is an ordinary NMOS body. Range -1e19 to -1e14, log. The page only offers p-type, because one log slider can't cross zero.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.t_ox: oxide thickness [cm]. 1e-6 is 10 nm. Range 1e-7 to 1e-5, log.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.t_si: how deep the silicon goes [cm]. Keep it several times deeper than the depletion region can reach, or the body contact gets in the way. Range 5e-5 to 1e-3, log.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.width: how wide the device is drawn [cm]. Nothing depends on it, since capacitance is reported per unit area. Range 1e-6 to 1e-4, log.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.nx: mesh points across the device, at least 2 [1]. Range 2 to 21.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.n_silicon: mesh points down through the silicon, counting the surface [1]. Range 21 to 401.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.n_oxide: mesh points through the oxide, counting the surface [1]. Range 2 to 41.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.h_min: the smallest mesh spacing, at the silicon surface [cm]. 5e-8 is 0.5 nm, fine enough for an inversion layer. Range 1e-8 to 1e-6, log.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.gate_voltage: voltage on the gate [V]. Range -2 to 2, the span the lesson sweeps.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.body_voltage: voltage on the bottom contact [V]. Range -2 to 2.
ddsim.device.mos_cap.mos_cap.work_function: the gate metal's work function [eV]. Defaults to n+ polysilicon, the usual NMOS gate. Range 4 to 5.3, from n+ to past p+ poly.

ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.L_gate: gate length [cm]. 1e-4 is 1 um. Range 5e-6 to 3e-4, log. It has to be more than twice lateral_diffusion or there's no channel left, so on the default device it stops at 2e-5. The short channel lesson goes down to 5e-6.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.sd_length: length of the source and of the drain [cm], from the outside edge to the edge of the gate. Range 3e-5 to 5.7e-5.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.contact_length: how much of the source and of the drain the metal contact covers [cm], measured in from the outside edge. Has to be less than sd_length. Range 5e-6 to 3e-5.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.substrate_doping: net doping of the body [cm^-3]. Negative means p-type. Range -1e19 to -1e14, log.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.sd_peak: doping at the surface of the source and drain [cm^-3]. Range 1e18 to 1e20, log.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.x_j: how deep the source and drain go [cm], measured where their doping falls to the body's. Range 2.5e-6 to 5e-5, log.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.lateral_diffusion: how far the source and drain creep sideways under the gate [cm]. The real channel is L_gate minus twice this. Range 1e-6 to 3e-5, log.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.t_ox: oxide thickness [cm]. 2e-6 is 20 nm. Range 1e-7 to 1e-5, log.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.t_si: how deep the silicon goes [cm], several times the depletion width. Range 5e-5 to 5e-4, log.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.n_contact: mesh columns under each contact [1]. Range 2 to 30.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.n_sd: mesh columns from a contact's edge to the gate's edge [1]. Range 9 to 55.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.n_channel: mesh columns in each half of the channel [1]. Range 11 to 59.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.n_silicon: mesh rows down through the silicon, counting the surface [1]. Range 17 to 285.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.n_oxide: mesh rows through the oxide, counting the surface [1]. Range 2 to 129.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.h_min_x: the smallest column spacing, at each junction [cm]. Range 1.2e-7 to 5e-6, log.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.h_min_y: the smallest row spacing, at the silicon surface [cm]. This is the mesh setting the drain current cares about most, because the thin inversion layer is the one thing on the device a mesh can miss. If you halve it, raise n_oxide too. Range 1e-9 to 1e-6, log.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.gate_voltage: voltage on the gate [V]. Range -1 to 2.5.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.drain_voltage: voltage on the drain [V]. Range -0.5 to 2.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.source_voltage: voltage on the source [V]. Range -0.5 to 0.5.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.body_voltage: voltage on the bottom contact [V]. Range -2 to 0.5, which stops short of forward biasing the body junctions.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.work_function: the gate's work function [eV]. Defaults to n+ polysilicon, the usual NMOS gate. Range 4 to 5.3.
ddsim.device.mosfet.nmos.degenerate: use Fermi-Dirac statistics instead of the simpler Boltzmann ones. On by default, because the source and drain are doped to 1e20 cm^-3, and there Boltzmann puts the Fermi level 30.5 mV off.

ddsim.device.stack.stack.regions: the regions in order from the left contact, at least two, with the doping changing at one boundary at least.
ddsim.device.stack.stack.n_nodes: how many mesh points the whole stack is cut into [1]. Range 51 to 1001. They get shared out between the junctions, so a stack with lots of junctions wants more.
ddsim.device.stack.stack.h_min: the smallest mesh spacing, at every junction [cm]. Range 1e-8 to 1e-6, log. It should be under half the Debye length: 20 nm at 1e16 but only 0.65 nm at 1e19, so the 1 nm default is too coarse for the most heavily doped regions.
ddsim.device.stack.stack.left_voltage: voltage on the left contact [V]. Range -5 to 1, the same as the diode's contacts.
ddsim.device.stack.stack.right_voltage: voltage on the right contact [V]. Range -5 to 1, the same as the left contact.

ddsim.device.drawing.drawing.blocks: rectangles of silicon and oxide, painted in order. Together they cover a rectangle whose lower left corner is the origin.
ddsim.device.drawing.drawing.electrodes: ohmic contacts on silicon and gates on oxide, each along a straight segment.
ddsim.device.drawing.drawing.nx: mesh points across the device [1]. Every edge you draw needs one, so a busy drawing needs more. Range 38 to 200.
ddsim.device.drawing.drawing.ny: mesh points up the device [1]. Range 22 to 400.
ddsim.device.drawing.drawing.h_min_x: the smallest column spacing, at every doping edge and every vertical silicon to oxide wall [cm]. Two edges closer than this get turned down. Range 4.1e-8 to 4.7e-6, log.
ddsim.device.drawing.drawing.h_min_y: the smallest row spacing, at every doping edge and every flat silicon to oxide interface [cm]. On a MOSFET the inversion layer is only a few nanometres thick, and this is what has to catch it. Range 1e-9 to 7.7e-7, log.
ddsim.device.drawing.drawing.degenerate: use Fermi-Dirac statistics instead of the simpler Boltzmann ones. On by default, because the starting drawing is the benchmark nmos, doped to 1e20 cm^-3 in its source and drain. With it off, any doping above 1e19 gets turned down.

ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.device: the device. Its own contact biases are overridden by the sweep.
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.contact: name of the contact to sweep.
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.voltages: the biases wanted [V], in the order they should be walked.
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.models: transport models, built from the device if None.
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.step: the biggest voltage step the solver takes on its way from one point on your list to the next [V].
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.min_step: give up once the continuation step falls below this [V]. None leaves it at the continuation default of a thousandth of step, which is about ten halvings. That is the right default for a sweep that is expected to succeed, and expensive for one that is expected to stall: every one of those ten halvings is a full failed solve at the Gummel budget. A caller who already knows the sweep may stall, or who only wants to know roughly where, should raise this.
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.start: the voltage the sweep starts from [V]. It's solved directly, not ramped up to.
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.max_iterations: how many Gummel cycles each point gets before it counts as failed [1].
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.update_tol: how small a whole Gummel cycle's change has to be before a point counts as solved [1].
ddsim.extract.iv.iv_sweep.on_frame: telemetry, or None to report nothing. Carries a GummelIteration per cycle, a ContinuationEvent per attempt and an IVFrame per point that lands. See phases/PHASE-7.md.

ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.device: the MOSFET, carrying the drain and body biases the curve is taken at. Its gate bias is overridden by the sweep.
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.voltages: the gate biases wanted [V], in the order to walk them.
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.contact: name of the terminal to sweep. The gate.
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.measure_at: name of the terminal to read the current at. The drain.
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.models: transport models, built from the device if None.
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.step: the biggest voltage step the solver takes on its way from one point on your list to the next [V].
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.min_step: give up once the step falls below this [V].
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.start: the gate voltage the sweep starts from [V]. It's solved directly, not ramped up to. The default is zero, which leaves an NMOS switched off.
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.max_iterations: how many Newton steps each point gets before it counts as failed [1].
ddsim.extract.iv.gate_sweep.on_frame: telemetry, or None to report nothing. Carries a NewtonIteration per iteration, a ContinuationEvent per attempt and an IVFrame per point that lands. No GummelIteration ever reaches it, because this path does not run Gummel at all.

ddsim.extract.cv.cv_sweep.device: the device. Its own bias at the swept contact is overridden.
ddsim.extract.cv.cv_sweep.contact: name of the terminal to sweep and to measure.
ddsim.extract.cv.cv_sweep.response: which carriers keep up with the small signal. With low_frequency both do. With high_frequency the minority carrier is held still, the way it is in a fast real measurement.
ddsim.extract.cv.cv_sweep.width: extent of the terminal transverse to the field [cm].
ddsim.extract.cv.cv_sweep.max_iterations: how many Newton steps each point gets before it counts as failed [1].
ddsim.extract.cv.cv_sweep.on_frame: telemetry, or None to report nothing. Carries a NewtonIteration per Poisson iteration and a CVFrame per point. There is no ContinuationEvent on this path: the points are independent solves rather than a ramp. See phases/PHASE-7.md.

ddsim.device.transport.TransportModels.f.device: the device, for its doping, temperature and scaling.
ddsim.device.transport.TransportModels.f.recombination: an explicit model, which overrides both the SRH default and the auger flag.
ddsim.device.transport.TransportModels.f.mobility: "constant" uses one mobility everywhere, the value for undoped silicon. "arora" slows carriers down wherever the doping is heavy, which is what real silicon does.
ddsim.device.transport.TransportModels.f.auger: add Auger recombination on top of the usual defect recombination. It only matters at very high carrier densities, so it's off by default.
ddsim.device.transport.TransportModels.f.field_dependent: cap how fast carriers can go in a strong field. This is what gives you velocity saturation. Off by default.
ddsim.device.transport.TransportModels.f.surface: slow down carriers pressed against the oxide, the way a real MOSFET channel does. Only works on a 2D device with an oxide on it. Off by default.
